disease: Hereditary antithrombin deficiency (antithrombin III deficiency / thrombophilia type 7)

emergence.disease: Hereditary antithrombin deficiency (antithrombin III deficiency / thrombophilia type 7)
emergence.summary: A single-gene SERPINC1 loss-of-function. SERPINC1 encodes antithrombin (antithrombin III), the principal plasma serpin BRAKE on the coagulation cascade: it forms irreversible 1:1 complexes with thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa (and IXa/XIa), an inhibition massively accelerated by heparin/heparan-sulfate. SERPINC1 LOF lowers functional antithrombin (type I quantitative deficiency) or yields a dysfunctional molecule (type II qualitative: reactive-site, heparin-binding, or pleiotropic variants), so thrombin and factor Xa are under-restrained -> the coagulation drive is pushed UP, giving heritable thrombophilia: recurrent venous thromboembolism, often early-onset, and pregnancy-associated thrombosis (homozygous complete deficiency is essentially embryonic-lethal, consistent with antithrombin being an essential brake). This is read on the kit's coagulation axis -- the SAME axis as haemophilia but driven the OPPOSITE way: haemophilia is the coagulation axis DOWN (a missing pro-coagulant cofactor/protease -> BLEEDING), antithrombin deficiency is the coagulation axis UP (a missing ANTI-coagulant brake -> CLOTTING). As a released brake the axis goes UP and the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN coagulation. The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm: antithrombin concentrate (plasma-derived, or recombinant antithrombin) -- which SUPPLIES the deficient serpin, restoring the brake on thrombin/factor Xa -- used for high-risk windows (surgery, delivery) on a background of therapeutic anticoagulation. Note the heparin caveat: heparin works by POTENTIATING antithrombin, so it is relatively less effective when antithrombin itself is deficient -- a reason the lead is to restore antithrombin and to use anticoagulants that act independently of it. Recorded as the THIRD serpin read in the kit -- after alpha-1-antitrypsin (SERPINA1, a protective-LEVEL axis DOWN: too little protease inhibitor) and hereditary angioedema (SERPING1/C1-INH, a bradykinin OVER-production axis UP) -- now completing the COAGULATION axis in BOTH directions (haemophilia DOWN vs antithrombin deficiency UP). The gamma read is of the SERPINC1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/structural (missense at the reactive site or heparin-binding domain, plus null alleles), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: coagulation-cascade restraint (antithrombin / SERPINC1 inhibition of thrombin + factor Xa; LOF -> under-restrained coagulation -> hypercoagulability / thrombophilia) -- the coagulation axis read as a released brake

per_gene.note: SERPINC1 encodes antithrombin (antithrombin III), the major plasma serpin that irreversibly inhibits thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa (also IXa/XIa) -- the principal endogenous BRAKE on coagulation, with its inhibitory rate hugely accelerated by heparin binding. Deficiency alleles are loss-of-function: type I (quantitative, reduced antithrombin) or type II (qualitative -- reactive-site, heparin-binding-site, or pleiotropic defects). Either way the brake on thrombin/Xa is weakened -> the coagulation drive is pushed UP -> thrombophilia. As a RELEASED BRAKE the pathological axis goes UP and the corrective levers LOWER it. Autosomal dominant for the heterozygous thrombophilia (homozygous quantitative deficiency is embryonic-lethal), 1q25.1 (OMIM 107300). NCBI official symbol SERPINC1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the reactive-site/heparin-binding missense and null lesions are outside the promoter firewall.

treatment_A_switch.disease: Hereditary antithrombin deficiency (antithrombin III deficiency / thrombophilia type 7)

levers.push_direction: supply antithrombin concentrate (replacing the deficient serpin) to restore inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa -> re-impose the coagulation brake -> lower the coagulation drive (net axis effect DOWN toward healthy)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of antithrombin restoration / thrombin-Xa inhibition not derived from sequence
levers.src: Recombinant antithrombin (ATryn) FDA 2009 / plasma-derived antithrombin (Thrombate III); peri-operative/peripartum use in hereditary antithrombin deficiency

levers.push_direction: block factor Xa directly with an oral anticoagulant (independent of antithrombin) -> lower the coagulation drive; an antithrombin-independent restrain arm preferred because heparin, which works THROUGH antithrombin, is relatively less effective when antithrombin is deficient
levers.agent_class: direct factor Xa inhibitor (e.g. rivaroxaban / apixaban)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of anticoagulation not derived from sequence
levers.src: EINSTEIN/AMPLIFY DOAC programmes (factor Xa inhibition in venous thromboembolism); antithrombin-independent mechanism

levers.push_direction: lower the vitamin-K-dependent procoagulant factors (II, VII, IX, X) with a vitamin-K antagonist -> reduce the coagulation drive (long-term secondary prevention)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree/target-INR of anticoagulation not derived from sequence
levers.src: Long-standing anticoagulation for inherited thrombophilia / recurrent VTE

lead_corrective_lever.push_direction: supply antithrombin concentrate (replacing the deficient serpin) to restore inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa -> re-impose the coagulation brake -> lower the coagulation drive (net axis effect DOWN toward healthy)
lead_corrective_lever.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of antithrombin restoration / thrombin-Xa inhibition not derived from sequence
lead_corrective_lever.src: Recombinant antithrombin (ATryn) FDA 2009 / plasma-derived antithrombin (Thrombate III); peri-operative/peripartum use in hereditary antithrombin deficiency

modelling.grade: [F] ordering forced (over-shoot) ; delta/treat_frac documented choices ; realised magnitude [O]

treatment_A_switch.firewall: levers are DIRECTION + cited agent CLASS; not dose/potency/efficacy/safety, not a recommendation to treat any individual.

falsifiers.claim: SERPINC1 LOF (loss of the antithrombin brake) raises coagulation drive (axis UP -> thrombophilia)
falsifiers.falsifier: a SERPINC1 LOF allele that LOWERED thrombin/factor-Xa activity or REDUCED thrombosis risk would refute the released-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: functional antithrombin activity and thrombin-/factor-Xa-generation assays in carriers vs controls, and the epidemiological venous-thromboembolism risk associated with antithrombin deficiency

falsifiers.claim: restraining coagulation (restoring antithrombin / anticoagulation) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if supplying antithrombin concentrate or anticoagulating RAISED thrombin generation or thrombosis, the restrain lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: thrombin-generation / anti-Xa response and clinical thrombosis incidence on antithrombin replacement plus anticoagulation in hereditary antithrombin deficiency
